Antibodies can develop in patients given recom- binant granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factors. The antibodies have been reported to occur more commonly, and in higher titres, in patients who are not immunocompromised com- pared with those who are.1,2 Although some binding antibodies are non-neutralising and have no apparent clinical effect,3 neu- tralising antibodies can reduce the efficacy of the colony-stimu- lating factor in repeated treatment cycles.1,2 However, antibodies have been reported to become undetectable after a number of weeks2 and do not appear to have long-term effects.1 Cross-reac- tivity between different granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimu- lating factors has been reported,1-3 and antibody formation may also be product dependent.2 1.
